s1.syndrome_frame: Bilateral ocular inflammation with recent onset of blurred vision and ocular irritation, following a systemic illness with fever and arthralgia
salient_findings: Stromal immune ring formation with underlying keratic precipitates
Positive Chikungunya virus PCR result in aqueous tap
key_facts: Patient is a teenage girl from Saint-Martin
Presented with bilateral blurred vision and ocular irritation
Experienced fever and severe arthralgia one month earlier
Recently acquired periorbital hyperpigmentation
Ocular history negative for trauma and previous inflammation
Primary HIV infection, tuberculosis, sarcoidosis, and syphilis had been ruled out
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 OU
Slitlamp biomicroscopy revealed bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography confirmed localized anterior stromal infiltrate
Aqueous tap PCR results were positive for Chikungunya virus
IgM CHIKV serologic test was positive

shortlist.label: Chikungunya virus ocular infection
shortlist.why_kept: Positive PCR results for Chikungunya virus in aqueous tap and positive IgM CHIKV serologic test

shortlist.label: Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ocular inflammation with stromal immune ring formation and keratic precipitates

shortlist.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation, although PCR results were negative for human herpesviruses

shortlist.label: Varicella-zoster virus keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ocular inflammation and recent onset of blurred vision, although PCR results were negative for varicella-zoster virus

shortlist.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ocular inflammation, recent onset of blurred vision, and periorbital hyperpigmentation

raw.rationale: The patient's aqueous tap PCR results were positive for Chikungunya virus and the IgM CHIKV serologic test was also positive, indicating a recent infection. The patient's symptoms, including bilateral blurred vision, ocular irritation, and recent fever and arthralgia, are consistent with Chikungunya virus ocular infection.

rejected.label: Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not match the typical presentation of Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis, which is a chronic condition with heterochromia of the iris and characteristic findings on slitlamp examination.

rejected.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
rejected.why: The aqueous tap PCR results were negative for human herpesviruses 1 and 2, making Herpes simplex keratitis unlikely.

rejected.label: Varicella-zoster virus keratitis
rejected.why: The aqueous tap PCR results were negative for varicella-zoster virus, making Varicella-zoster virus keratitis unlikely.

rejected.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not match the typical presentation of Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease, which is a systemic condition with granulomatous uveitis and characteristic skin, hair, and auditory findings.
